questions.stem: On a workgroup laptop that has never joined a domain, an admin opens gpedit.msc and sets a 10-minute screen lock. Which description BEST classifies this change?

options.text: Local group policy for this one laptop
options.rationale: Correct: gpedit.msc edits local group policy, whose scope is the single machine it is set on.

options.text: A domain GPO pushed to the computers in an OU
options.rationale: A domain GPO comes from Active Directory, and this laptop has never joined a domain.

options.text: A site-level GPO from Active Directory
options.rationale: Site GPOs also come from Active Directory and reach the computers in a site, not one standalone laptop.

options.text: An SELinux rule enforced by the Linux kernel
options.rationale: SELinux is mandatory access control on Linux, not a Windows policy setting.

questions.explanation: Local group policy configures a single computer, is edited with gpedit.msc, and needs no domain. Domain, site, and OU GPOs come from Active Directory, reach many computers, and override local settings where they conflict.
questions.discriminator_tested: Scope: local policy covers one machine, while Active Directory GPOs cover many.
